statement: Find all triplets $(x,y,p)$ of positive integers such that $p$ is a prime number and $\dfrac{xy^3}{x+y}=p$.

Let $P(x)=ax^3+(b-a)x^2-(c+b)x+c$ and $Q(x)=x^4+(b-1)x^3+(a-b)x^2-(c+a)x+c$ be polynomials of $x$ with $a,b,c$ non-zero real numbers and $b>0$. If $P(x)$ has three distinct real roots $x_0,x_1,x_2$ which are also roots of $Q(x)$ then: A) Prove that $abc>28$. B) If $a,b,c$ are non-zero integers with $b>0$, find all their possible values.

Given a triangle $ABC$ with $\angle B=105^\circ$. Let $D$ be a point on $BC$ such that $\angle BDA=45^\circ$. A) If $D$ is the midpoint of $BC$, prove that $\angle C=30^\circ$. B) If $\angle C=30^\circ$, prove that $D$ is the midpoint of $BC$.

figure_description: Square divided into unit squares with triangle ABD and circular arcs at vertices
statement: A square $ABCD$ with side-length $n$ is divided into $n^2$ small (fundamental) squares. The squares' vertices inside or on the boundary of triangle $ABD$ are connected with arcs. Starting from $A$, we move only upwards or to the right. Each movement is along segments defined by the fundamental squares and arcs of the circles. How many possible paths are there to reach $C$?
